messages.subject: Model predictions when scaling covariates
parts:
Hello,
I am fitting an occupancy model with a covariate (elevation) for detection
prob:

> m.cespa.el<- occu(~elevation_m ~1, umf.cespa)

However, apparently there was a problem:

>m.cespa.el
Call:
occu(formula = ~elevation_m ~ 1, data = umf.cespa)

Occupancy:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
0.209 0.232 0.904 0.366

Detection:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) -2.14947 NaN NaN NaN
elevation_m -0.00055 NaN NaN NaN

AIC: 472.1859
Warning message:
In sqrt(diag(vcov(obj))) : NaNs produced

So I scaled elevation:

>m.cespa.el<- occu(~scale(elevation_m) ~1, umf.cespa)
>m.cespa.el
Call:
occu(formula = ~scale(elevation_m) ~ 1, data = umf.cespa)

Occupancy:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
0.687 0.488 1.41 0.159

Detection:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) -3.370 0.221 -15.23 2.39e-52
scale(elevation_m) 0.639 0.183 3.48 4.98e-04

AIC: 452.1061

Which looks much better:

Now, I want to predict det. probabilities at different elevations so:

>elev.pred<-data.frame(elevation_m=seq(300,1700,100))
>predict(m.cespa.el,"det",newdata=elev.pred,appendData=T)

Predicted SE lower upper elevation_m

If not correct how do I back transform to the original units for the

Jorge

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Model predictions when scaling covariates
parts:
hi Jorge,
to make predictions you also have to use the scaled covariate, so
either generate a grid from roughly -2 to +2 or else figure out
provide a specific set of points standardized using the observed mean
and sd values. i.e., if xgrid is a set of elevations then you need to
do this:

xgridstd<- (xgrid - xbardata)/sddata

hope that makes sense.

regards
andy

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Model predictions when scaling covariates
parts:
Hi Jorge,

In this case, because you used scale() in the formula, predict automatically does what Andy suggested. So your predictions are "correct" albeit incredibly low.

Richard



elev.pred<-data.frame(elevation_m=seq(-2,2,100))
E.p <- predict(m.cespa.el,"det",newdata=elev.pred,appendData=T)
E.p$elev.back <- elev.pred$
